name: enumerate-iam - AWS IAM Permission Enumeration
description: enumerate-iam brute-forces AWS IAM permissions by attempting every API call and recording which ones succeed. Given a set of AWS credentials, it determines what the identity can actually do across all AWS services. Essential for assessing compromised AWS credentials and finding privilege escalation paths.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  git clone https://github.com/andresriancho/enumerate-iam
  cd enumerate-iam
  pip3 install -r requirements.txt

=== RUN ===
  python3 enumerate-iam.py --access-key AKIA... --secret-key wJa...
  # With session token (for temporary credentials):
  python3 enumerate-iam.py --access-key AKIA... --secret-key wJa... --session-token FwoG...

=== WHAT IT DOES ===
- Calls sts:GetCallerIdentity first (always works)
- Then brute forces ~4000+ API calls across all services
- Records which calls return data vs AccessDenied
- Output shows allowed actions

=== ALTERNATIVE: Pacu ===
  # Pacu is a full AWS exploitation framework:
  pacu
  > set_keys
  > run iam__enum_permissions
  > run iam__privesc_scan

=== COMMON ESCALATION PATHS ===
- iam:CreatePolicyVersion (change own permissions)
- iam:AttachUserPolicy (attach admin policy)
- iam:PassRole + lambda:CreateFunction (exec as role)
- sts:AssumeRole to cross-account roles
- ssm:SendCommand to EC2 instances

defense.why_it_works: AWS IAM permissions are not visible through a single API call. The tool brute-forces all service endpoints to discover what actions the credential is authorized to perform. AccessDenied errors are expected and do not trigger lockouts.
defense.prerequisites: Valid AWS access key, secret key, and optionally session token.
defense.impact: Complete visibility into compromised credentials capabilities; identifies privilege escalation paths.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.004] Massive spike in API calls across many services; most returning AccessDenied; CloudTrail AccessDenied anomaly.
defense.artifacts: CloudTrail logs showing thousands of API calls with AccessDenied errors from a single identity.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail errorCode="AccessDenied"
| stats dc(eventName) as unique_apis, count by userIdentity.arn
| where unique_apis > 100
| sort -unique_apis
defense.sentinel_kql:
AWSCloudTrail
| where ErrorCode == "AccessDenied"
| summarize UniqueAPIs=dcount(EventName), TotalCalls=count() by UserIdentityArn
| where UniqueAPIs > 100
defense.prevention: Enable CloudTrail anomaly detection; alert on high AccessDenied rates; use AWS GuardDuty; implement least privilege; rotate compromised credentials immediately.

detections.name: AWS IAM permission enumeration brute force
detections.logic:
AWSCloudTrail
| where ErrorCode == "AccessDenied"
| summarize UniqueAPIs=dcount(EventName), TotalCalls=count(), Services=dcount(EventSource) by UserIdentityArn, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where UniqueAPIs > 50 and Services > 10
detections.false_positives: Poorly configured automation with overly broad API calls
detections.tuning: Adjust threshold based on environment; correlate with known automation identities
